Fixed random effects: formulas parameter, e.g. fform = b1 + b2 ~ treatment rform = b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant, nlme::nlme; random effects correlated across parameters, several terms, nested crossed grouping factors random slopes, integrated Laplace approximation. Autocorrelation: AR(1) continuous-time AR(1) residuals within individuals, correlation = corCAR1(form = ~ day | plant), correlation structures nlme. Inference: profile likelihood, Wald parametric bootstrap confidence intervals; likelihood ratio tests chi-square, F parametric bootstrap p-values; information criteria; pairwise comparisons curves simultaneous confidence intervals; small-sample t F inference gaussian models without random effects. Derived quantities: times reach percentage asymptote given response (timeto()), maximum growth rate, timing fraction asymptote reached (maxrate()), standard errors confidence intervals. text: main function gcTMB(). response curve f(t) explanatory variable t, usually time. first curves (logistic, Gompertz, Hill, Weibull, beta, normal gamma) sigmoid growth curves, often used agronomy ecology, e.g. growth plants, crops animals season. Chapman-Richards Wykoff curves height-diameter models, common forestry, diameter trees t. Preece-Baines curve model human growth height childhood puberty. b1 asymptote approached late times (maximum, reached end growth b3, beta curves; adult height Preece-Baines), slope linear model, asymptote. Phi standard normal distribution function, Fgamma(t; k, theta) distribution function gamma distribution shape k scale theta. Hill, Weibull gamma curves positive times. links parameters can chosen, e.g. link = c(b1 = "log", b3 = "inverse"), identity (default), log, logit (b1) inverse (b3 logistic Gompertz models, rate 1/b3) links. default, logistic, Gompertz, Hill, Weibull, normal gamma curves f(t) truncated threshold time b4: shifted zero b4 rescaled keep asymptote b1, b1 (f(t) - f(b4))/(b1 - f(b4)) t > b4, response zero b4. b4 fixed 0, curve starts zero t = 0, unless estimated fix = c(b4 = FALSE); truncated = FALSE gives curves without truncation. six models asymmetry parameter b5 > 0, fixed 1 (curves ) unless estimated fix = c(b5 = FALSE): logistic model becomes Richards curve b1 / (1 + b5 exp(-(t - b2)/b3))^(1/b5), Hill model b1 / (1 + (b2/t)b3)b5, Weibull, normal gamma models b1 (f(t)/b1)^b5, power curve relative asymptote, Gompertz model b1 (1 - (1 - exp(-exp(-(t - b2)/b3)))^b5), power survival function. curves never truncated, general growth curves asymmetry b5. "beta" continues curve Yin et al. beyond b3, back zero 2 b3 - b2, responses decline maximum; "beta_capped" stays b1 b3 , beta sigmoid growth function Yin et al. Forestry: Chapman-Richards Wykoff curves height-diameter models trees (models M8 M9 Ciceu et al. 2020), diameter t. intercept b4 fixed 0 unless given start estimated fix = c(b4 = FALSE), e.g. breast height 1.3 m, start = c(b4 = 1.3). Chapman-Richards curve Richards curve negative asymmetry.
